images.title: Look at the last two
images.purpose: Show that multiples of 4 can be spotted from the last two digits.
images.composition: Three numbers stacked in a centred column with a single line below, lots of white space.
images.exact_structure: Three numbers stacked and evenly spaced: 332, 1732, 2032. In each, the last two digits 32 are reddish purple #CC79A7 and the rest teal #0072B2. Below, centred: one line of text. Exactly 3 numbers.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any digit other than 32 coloured reddish purple
images.takeaway: If the last two digits make a multiple of 4, the number is a multiple of 4.
images.description: Three numbers whose last two digits are 32, highlighted, each a multiple of 4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the last two digits in each number and say what they share.

image_decisions.why: Highlighting the last two digits is the one picture idea.
